ESV.1: So Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the Negeb.
ESV.2: Now Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
ESV.3: And he journeyed on from the Negeb as far as Bethel to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
ESV.4: to the place where he had made an altar at the first. And there Abram called upon the name of the LORD.
ESV.5: And Lot, who went with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents,
ESV.6: so that the land could not support both of them dwelling together; for their possessions were so great that they could not dwell together,
ESV.7: and there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were dwelling in the land.
ESV.8: Then Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herdsmen and my herdsmen, for we are kinsmen.
ESV.9: Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you take the left hand, then I will go to the right, or if you take the right hand, then I will go to the left.”
ESV.10: And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw that the Jordan Valley was well watered everywhere like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, in the direction of Zoar. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
ESV.11: So Lot chose for himself all the Jordan Valley, and Lot journeyed east. Thus they separated from each other.
ESV.12: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled among the cities of the valley and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
ESV.13: Now the men of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against the LORD.
ESV.14: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, “Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,
ESV.15: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.
ESV.16: I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth, so that if one can count the dust of the earth, your offspring also can be counted.
ESV.17: Arise, walk through the length and the breadth of the land, for I will give it to you.”
ESV.18: So Abram moved his tent and came and settled by the oaks  of Mamre, which are at Hebron, and there he built an altar to the LORD.

NASB.1: So Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev, he and his wife and all that belonged to him, and Lot with him.
NASB.2: Now Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver and in gold.
NASB.3: He went on his journeys from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
NASB.4: to the place of the altar which he had made there formerly; and there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
NASB.5: Now Lot, who went with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
NASB.6: And the land could not sustain them while dwelling together, for their possessions were so great that they were not able to remain together.
NASB.7: And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. Now the Canaanite and the Perizzite were dwelling then in the land.
NASB.8: So Abram said to Lot, 'Please let there be no strife between you and me, nor between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brothers.
NASB.9: 'Is not the whole land before you? Please separate from me; if [to] the left, then I will go to the right; or if [to] the right, then I will go to the left.'
NASB.10: Lot lifted up his eyes and saw all the valley of the Jordan, that it was well watered everywhere-- [this was] before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah-- like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt as you go to Zoar.
NASB.11: So Lot chose for himself all the valley of the Jordan, and Lot journeyed eastward. Thus they separated from each other.
NASB.12: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled in the cities of the valley, and moved his tents as far as Sodom.
NASB.13: Now the men of Sodom were wicked exceedingly and sinners against the LORD.
NASB.14: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, 'Now lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward;
NASB.15: for all the land which you see, I will give it to you and to your descendants forever.
NASB.16: 'I will make your descendants as the dust of the earth, so that if anyone can number the dust of the earth, then your descendants can also be numbered.
NASB.17: 'Arise, walk about the land through its length and breadth; for I will give it to you.'
NASB.18: Then Abram moved his tent and came and dwelt by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and there he built an altar to the LORD.

CSB17.1: Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev <sup>ⓒ</sup>  — he, his wife, and all he had, and Lot with him.
CSB17.2: Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.

CSB17.7: and there was quarreling between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. <sup>ⓕ</sup> (At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land.) <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.8: So Abram said to Lot, “Please, let’s not have quarreling between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen, since we are relatives. <sup>[1]</sup>

CSB17.10: Lot looked out and saw that the entire plain <sup>[2]</sup> of the Jordan <sup>ⓗ</sup> as far as <sup>[3]</sup> Zoar <sup>ⓘ</sup> was well watered everywhere like the LORD’s garden <sup>ⓙ</sup> and the land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) <sup>ⓚ</sup>

CSB17.12: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, but Lot lived in the cities on the plain and set up his tent near Sodom.
CSB17.13: (Now the men of Sodom were evil, sinning immensely <sup>[4]</sup> against the LORD.) <sup>ⓛ</sup>

AMP.1: So Abram went up out of Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot [his nephew] with him, into the Negev (the South country of Judah).
AMP.2: Now Abram was extremely rich in livestock and in silver and in gold.
AMP.3: He journeyed on from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
AMP.4: where he had first built an altar; and there Abram called on the name of the LORD [in prayer].
AMP.5: But Lot, who went with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
AMP.6: Now the land was not able to support them [that is, sustain all their grazing and water needs] while they lived near one another, for their possessions were too great for them to stay together.
AMP.7: And there was strife and quarreling between the herdsmen of Abram's cattle and the herdsmen of Lot's cattle. Now the Canaanite and the Perizzite were living in the land at that same time [making grazing of the livestock difficult].
AMP.8: So Abram said to Lot, "Please let there be no strife and disagreement between you and me, nor between your herdsmen and my herdsmen, because we are relatives.
AMP.9: Is not the entire land before you? Please separate [yourself] from me. If you take the left, then I will go to the right; or if you choose the right, then I will go to the left."
AMP.10: So Lot looked and saw that the valley of the Jordan was well watered everywhere—this was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah; [it was all] like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as you go to Zoar [at the south end of the Dead Sea].
AMP.11: Then Lot chose for himself all the valley of the Jordan, and he traveled east. So they separated from each other.
AMP.12: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot settled in the cities of the valley and camped as far as Sodom and lived there.
AMP.13: But the men of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinful against the LORD [unashamed in their open sin before Him].
AMP.14: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot had left him, "Now lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are standing, northward and southward and eastward and westward;
AMP.15: for all the land which you see I will give to you and to your descendants forever.
AMP.16: I will make your descendants [as numerous] as the dust of the earth, so that if a man could count the [grains of] dust of the earth, then your descendants could also be counted.
AMP.17: Arise, walk (make a thorough reconnaissance) around in the land, through its length and its width, for I will give it to you."
AMP.18: Then Abram broke camp and moved his tent, and came and settled by the [grove of the great] terebinths (oak trees) of Mamre [the Amorite], which are in Hebron, and there he built an altar to [honor] the LORD.

NLT.1: So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned.
NLT.2: (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.)
NLT.3: From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before.
NLT.4: This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the LORD again.
NLT.5: Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents.
NLT.6: But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together.
NLT.7: So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.)
NLT.8: Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives!
NLT.9: The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.”
NLT.10: Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the LORD or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
NLT.11: Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram.
NLT.12: So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain.
NLT.13: But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the LORD.
NLT.14: After Lot had gone, the LORD said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction — north and south, east and west.
NLT.15: I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants as a permanent possession.
NLT.16: And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted!
NLT.17: Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.”
NLT.18: So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the LORD.

NET.1: So Abram went up from Egypt into the Negev. He took his wife and all his possessions with him, as well as Lot.
NET.2: (Now Abram was very wealthy in livestock, silver, and gold.)
NET.3: And he journeyed from place to place from the Negev as far as Bethel. He returned to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai.
NET.4: This was the place where he had first built the altar, and there Abram worshiped the LORD.
NET.5: Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.
NET.6: But the land could not support them while they were living side by side. Because their possessions were so great, they were not able to live alongside one another.
NET.7: So there were quarrels between Abram’s herdsmen and Lot’s herdsmen. (Now the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land at that time.)
NET.8: Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no quarreling between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are close relatives.

NET.11: Lot chose for himself the whole region of the Jordan and traveled toward the east. So the relatives separated from each other.
NET.12: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, but Lot settled among the cities of the Jordan plain and pitched his tents next to Sodom.
NET.13: (Now the people of Sodom were extremely wicked rebels against the LORD.)
NET.14: After Lot had departed, the LORD said to Abram, “Look from the place where you stand to the north, south, east, and west.
NET.15: I will give all the land that you see to you and your descendants forever.
NET.16: And I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone is able to count the dust of the earth, then your descendants also can be counted.
NET.17: Get up and walk throughout the land, for I will give it to you.”
NET.18: So Abram moved his tents and went to live by the oaks of Mamre in Hebron, and he built an altar to the LORD there.

NIV.1:
Abram and Lot Separate
So Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev, with his wife and everything he had, and Lot went with him.
NIV.2: Abram had become very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold.
NIV.3: From the Negev he went from place to place until he came to Bethel, to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had been earlier
NIV.4: and where he had first built an altar. There Abram called on the name of the Lord.
NIV.5: Now Lot, who was moving about with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
NIV.6: But the land could not support them while they stayed together, for their possessions were so great that they were not able to stay together.
NIV.7: And quarreling arose between Abram’s herdsmen and the herdsmen of Lot. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.
NIV.8: So Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not have any quarreling between you and me, or between your herdsmen and mine, for we are brothers.
NIV.9: Is not the whole land before you? Let’s part company. If you go to the left, I’ll go to the right; if you go to the right, I’ll go to the left.”
NIV.10: Lot looked up and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan was well watered, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt, toward Zoar. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
NIV.11: So Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan and set out toward the east. The two men parted company:
NIV.12: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived among the cities of the plain and pitched his tents near Sodom.
NIV.13: Now the men of Sodom were wicked and were sinning greatly against the Lord.
NIV.14: The Lord said to Abram after Lot had parted from him, “Lift up your eyes from where you are and look north and south, east and west.
NIV.15: All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring forever.
NIV.16: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone could count the dust, then your offspring could be counted.
NIV.17: Go, walk through the length and breadth of the land, for I am giving it to you.”
NIV.18: So Abram moved his tents and went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the Lord.
